gen-gf-syne-tactile-rubik: Rubik reads big and soft, its round lowercase friendly at any size. Over a long page it stays easy going, while Syne Tactile adds a broad-nibbed pen stroke that never quite curls shut.
gen-gf-tai-heritage-pro-fs-bespoke-sans: Tai Heritage Pro draws its strokes like tapered glass rods, with sweeping curves that stay open. And Bespoke Sans follows with sharp, refined lines, leaving generous gaps where curves meet the stem, so a long stretch of text moves smoothly.
gen-gf-tajawal-fs-literata: Approachable is the first word for Tajawal, whose open bowls welcome the eye without any fuss. But Literata brings a bookish weight, thin lines sturdy and thick ones slightly heavier, so reading on carries on comfortably.
gen-gf-tasa-explorer-fs-literata: Professional but light, TASA Explorer pulls its terminals well back. Literata is the one to linger over, a text serif with sturdy thin lines and wide, unclosed curves made for steady reading.
gen-gf-tasa-orbiter-fs-literata: TASA Orbiter has a wide funnel-like throat in its e and a modern, low-key manner. Literata sits against it as the bookish one, sturdy thin lines and heavier thick ones, so the two feel like a quiet conversation.
gen-gf-tauri-fs-literata: Contemporary and plain, Tauri keeps its letters simple and modern at the top. Yet Literata gives the page a sophisticated, bookish voice, with wide-mouthed curves and sturdy thin lines under the heading.
gen-gf-taviraj-fs-bespoke-sans: Bespoke Sans reads sharp and refined, with generous space where its curves meet the stem. And Taviraj adds a lightly shaded texture above, so a modest heading size lets that texture show.
gen-gf-teachers-fs-literata: Teachers has a pen-plotter smoothness, every stroke ending at the same measured thickness, with open bowls. Literata then reads like a classic serif, sturdy and bookish.
gen-gf-telex-fs-literata: Literata brings a sophisticated, bookish feel, with sturdy thin lines and curves that stay wide open. And Telex sits above in sans-serif form, its small round letters generously unclosed, so the two share an easy openness.
gen-gf-tenor-sans-fs-literata: Tenor Sans is defined by distinctly open letter mouths and a mellow modulation that is gentle on the eye. Literata follows in serif form, bookish and sturdy, so the page feels settled.
